thesis: Modal voltron: land either commander and keep it alive, let it tax every card that moves (Shabraz takes a counter and 1 life per draw, Brallin a counter and 1 damage to each opponent per discard), and win by 21 commander damage, with a wheel held until a commander is out as the finisher that turns one turn's hand into the kill.

stages.label: PAY FOR A COMMANDER, THEN FOR THE TURN
stages.what_it_does: Thirty-six lands (34 entries, three Mountains) plus Sol Ring, Arcane Signet, two Signets, Talisman of Creativity and Smothering Tithe pay for a 4- or 5-mana commander, then for equip costs, a double-strike grant and a held wheel on the same turn. The declared ramp group (those six) is in 36.4% of opening sevens and drawn by turn six in 69.1% of games (deck-audit). deck-facts: land sources R 30 / U 23 / W 20 against targets R 36 / U 22 / W 22, and 14 lands can enter tapped; red, the colour of Brallin and every wheel but three, sits furthest under its target. Smothering Tithe is filed here because Treasure is what it makes, and a symmetrical wheel is seven opponent draws per seat for it to tax; that pairing has no passing stack in which Tithe is on the battlefield. Several lands do a second job, filed here because making mana is what they do every game: Command Beacon returns a commander to hand (a tax reset), Otawara bounces by channel, Talon Gates of Madara phases a creature out, and Raugrin Triome and Glittering Massif cycle, which is a discard for Brallin (stack 003: a cost discard triggers him). powertune-v1 put Sea of Clouds and Adarkar Wastes in for Mystic Monastery and Opal Palace.

stages.label: A COMMANDER ON THE BATTLEFIELD
stages.what_it_does: The engine does not pay until Shabraz (5 mana, flying) or Brallin (4 mana) has resolved and survived: without one a loot or a wheel pays no commander, and the multipliers lose the triggers they are in the deck to multiply, which is why the pilot holds wheels until a commander is out. Shabraz turns each card drawn into a +1/+1 counter and 1 life; Brallin turns each card discarded into a +1/+1 counter and 1 damage to each opponent. The two hand each other evasion by oracle text: Brallin's {R} gives a Shark trample and Shabraz is a Shark Bird; Shabraz's {W/U} gives a Human flying and Brallin is a Human Shaman. The deck is modal: either one alone can be the 21-commander-damage threat, so the ignition is redundant, not single, and each removal adds 2 to that commander's tax. Both start in the command zone, so drawing them is never the constraint; casting and keeping them is. goldfish_metrics.json (10,000 games, the current decklist sha): Shabraz is cast by turn six in 87.7% (mean turn 4.928, median 5), Brallin in 95.8% (mean 4.015), and both are on the battlefield by turn six in 87.5%. The goldfish casts each once and has no removal, so these are a ceiling on the ignition, not its survival; protection is drawn by turn six in 84.2% (deck-audit). goldfish_targets still calls a WHEEL 'the ignition' and marks it `required`; that reading is the one this model replaces (proposed_goldfish_edits[0]).

both commanders out: the wheel kill runs through both triggers

stages.label: EVERY CARD THAT MOVES
stages.what_it_does: Steady fuel between wheels: a loot pays both commanders at once (a draw for Shabraz, a discard for Brallin) without emptying the hand. Repeatable loots: Kitsa ({T}), Mary Read and Anne Bonny ({T}, plus a Treasure on a discarded Pirate or Island), Teferi, Master of Time (+1 at instant speed), Jeskai Ascendancy (per noncreature spell), Ledger Shredder (connive). One-shot loots: Faithless Looting, Frantic Search, Sorcerer Class's entry. Draw engines that tax opponents: Rhystic Study, Mystic Remora, Faerie Mastermind, Ghostly Pilferer. Discard converters: Rielle draws as many as you discarded the first time each turn, and Inti discards on attack for a counter, trample and an impulse draw. Two narrow tutors aim the flow: Idyllic Tutor for an enchantment (the multipliers live there) and Stoneforge Mystic for any of the four Equipment. The standing-draw group (nine cards) is in 49.8% of opening sevens and drawn by turn six in 82.3%; the discard-converter group (Inti, Mako, Mary Read, Rielle) in 25.8% and 54.5% (deck-audit). Kitsa is proven on boards of 99 cards twice: stack 007 has its loot pay Brallin a counter and a ping, and stack 010 has it copy Wheel of Fortune. Stack 006 shows its loot between first-strike and regular damage making Shabraz 10 + 11 = 21, but that board's double strike was the cut Fireshrieker. There is no dedicated fodder stage: the deck eats its own hand. Cards that pay for being discarded (the cyclers Magmakin, Mako, Raugrin Triome and Glittering Massif; Mary Read's Treasure on a discarded Pirate) are filed under their other job.

stages.label: MAKE EACH CARD WORTH MORE
stages.what_it_does: The commanders convert one card into one counter or one ping; these nine raise what each card is worth. Counters: Lae'zel adds one to every counter placement (stack 008: Windfall gives Brallin 10 counters for 5 discards and Shabraz 14 for 7 draws). Draws: Bard, King of Dale and Teferi's Ageless Insight turn every draw into two except the first one in each of your draw steps, so a main-phase wheel's draws are all doubled; Consecrated Sphinx draws two per opponent draw, so a symmetrical wheel is 21 triggers (stack 009: 49 cards, Shabraz 52/52, and the cleanup discard of 42 fires Brallin past 40 at every seat). Knowledge Is Power makes the draw turn a pump turn for the whole team. Damage, on Brallin's pings: Torbran adds 2 per red-source event to an opponent (stack 005: seven pings, 21 to each opponent, not a kill from 40), Artist's Talent at level 3 adds 2 per noncombat event (stack 004), and with Torbran, Gratuitous Violence and Fiery Emancipation all out one ping is at least 8 per opponent, since each opponent orders the replacements (stack 007). The amplifier group (Torbran, Gratuitous Violence, Fiery Emancipation) is in 19.9% of opening sevens and drawn by turn six in 45.8%; Lae'zel alone in 7.1% and 18.1% (deck-audit, which names it the deck's one single-card point of failure for its target). Gratuitous Violence and Fiery Emancipation also multiply commander combat damage by oracle text; no passing stack resolves combat under them.

stages.label: THE SECOND COLLECTORS
stages.what_it_does: What the engine produces besides a large commander: three creatures that collect the same discard tax Brallin does. Glint-Horn Buccaneer deals 1 to each opponent per card discarded, a second Brallin (haste, and a {1}{R} loot while attacking). Magmakin Artillerist deals damage equal to the cards discarded to each opponent, once per discard event, and cycles for a ping of its own; answers-v1 brought it in for Jeska's Will. Marauding Mako grows a counter per card discarded and cycles. The declared second-damage group (Glint-Horn, Magmakin) is two cards: 13.7% of opening sevens, drawn by turn six in 33.1% (deck-audit marks it thin). Stack 004 resolves Magmakin's single blast for a seven-card discard as 7 to each opponent, 9 under Artist's Talent, beside Brallin's seven pings: 30 per seat, 40 to 10. No passing stack has Glint-Horn on the battlefield, so its doubling of a wheel's pings is oracle text only.

stages.label: KEEP THE COMMANDER, CLEAR THE LANE
stages.what_it_does: The whole engine is one creature that a single removal spell answers. Constant cover: Lightning Greaves (haste and shroud, equip 0) and Robe of Stars (phase out). Held cover: Flawless Maneuver and Deflecting Swat (free with a commander out), Loran's Escape, March of Swirling Mist, and the counters Negate, Stubborn Denial and Izzet Charm. Grand Abolisher shuts off responses on your own turn, which is the turn the wheel or the double-strike attack happens. Answers that clear a blocker or a hate piece: Swords to Plowshares, Get Lost, Chaos Warp, Prismari Command. The declared protection group (nine cards, counting Akroma's Will, Boros Charm and Brotherhood Regalia, which this model files under wincon) is in 49.8% of opening sevens and drawn by turn six in 84.2%; the answers group (nine) in 49.8% and 83.5% (deck-audit). Both price DRAWING a card, never using it at the right moment. No passing stack resolves any of these protecting a commander from removal; stacks 005, 008 and 010 hold Negate, Swords or Lightning Greaves only as cards in hand or on the board.

stages.label: TWENTY-ONE, OR THE WHEEL
stages.what_it_does: Two endings, and the pilot chooses between them each game. COMMANDER DAMAGE: a grown commander connects for 21. The kit: double strike from Shu Yun (pay {R/W}{R/W} per noncreature spell), Embercleave, Blade Historian, Boros Charm or Akroma's Will (which, with a commander out, also gives indestructible and protection from each colour); evasion from Brotherhood Regalia (can't be blocked, ward 2) or the commanders' own flying and trample grants. Stack 006 is the shape: a 10/10 double-striker that loots between strikes deals 10 + 11. THE WHEEL: a full-hand discard-and-draw with a commander out. Wheel of Fortune, Windfall, Reforge the Soul, Tolarian Winds (instant), Jace's Archivist (repeatable), Fateful Showdown (instant, plus damage equal to the hand), and the wheel modes of Collective Defiance and Incendiary Command. The wheel group is in 45.6% of opening sevens, drawn by turn three in 54.7% and by turn six in 73.4% (deck-audit), so the usual job is holding one, not finding one. A wheel pays one ping per card discarded, so its damage is the hand size: seven cards made 7 per seat (stack 001), a three-card hand copied by Kitsa made 3 + 7 = 10 (stack 010), and under Consecrated Sphinx the cleanup discard is the kill (stack 009). Paired with a second per-discard damage source it is drawn by turn six in 25.7%. A wheel also grows both commanders, so it feeds the first ending as well as being the second.

map_disagreements.why: The map files a wheel by the rest of its text: the five plain or near-plain wheels sit in Tutors, the two modal ones whose other modes deal damage (Collective Defiance, Incendiary Command) in Interaction, and Jace's Archivist, a creature with a tap ability, in Card Flow. To the engine all eight are one finisher, because a discard pays Brallin and a draw pays Shabraz whatever else the card says.

Embercleave, Blade Historian and Brotherhood Regalia read as Finishers; Boros Charm and Akroma's Will read as Interaction on their protective modes; Shu Yun reads as a body. All five do one job here: give a grown commander double strike or an unblocked lane. The voltron route is not visible in card text as a group.

The multipliers are replacement effects whose text names damage, counters or draws, and the map clusters on those nouns: the enchantments with Finishers, the creatures with Bodies, Artist's Talent (a loot at level 1) and Consecrated Sphinx (a draw engine) with Card Flow. What unites them, multiplying a commander trigger, is a relation to Brallin and Shabraz that no single card's text states.

Loot creatures (Kitsa, Mary Read, Rielle, Inti) cluster with Bodies on their type line; Faithless Looting and Frantic Search sit with the wheels in Tutors. They do the same job here, paying both commanders at once.

Lightning Greaves, Robe of Stars and Grand Abolisher sit in Finishers beside the voltron Equipment and Abolisher's turn-lock, Chaos Warp in Tutors (it reveals off the top of a library); everything else that protects the window sits in Interaction.

The two Signets and Talisman of Creativity sit in Card Flow, not with Sol Ring and Arcane Signet in Ramp. A reading, not a measurement: their activated two-colour text sits nearer the blue loot cards than the colourless rocks do.
